parsed.explanation: Combined regime is hostile and traveller-facing: federal passport/visa rules force binary markers, entry officers can refuse cases or trigger lifetime fraud ineligibility for perceived misrepresentation. Many state/province and federal-funded facilities ban gender-congruent use; a few criminalise it as trespass, with one arrest and men's-ward hold. If detained, immigration/corrections policies permit hormone removal, forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Courts and anti-discrimination/hate-crime laws provide partial recourse but institutions enforce restrictions; minors face youth-care bans and school directives. Not execution/imprisonment highly likely, but severe.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order/visa cable: sex at birth binary, X no new; mismatch or doubt -> refuse/request evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation -> possible permanent ineligibility under fraud ground; foreign detentions reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; litigation ongoing; legal FAQ; waivers limited but permanent bar never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch can escalate into secondary screening, refusal, detention, fraud inquiry, and state document/facility exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Visa detentions and facility men's-ward hold documented. Reported immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; corrections conversion-style hormone removal. Custody-abuse detail single-sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No operational traveller-facing protection documented; courts may review, but hostile custody practices appear enforced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing at border/facility can lead to custody; federal custody policy shapes treatment of detained travellers.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal bar on gender-congruent government-funded single-sex facilities; many states ban in schools/government; some private; 4 criminal trespass; arrest/24h men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No nationwide criminalisation; many jurisdictions no ban; trespass requires willful entry and refusal to depart, not automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility policy + state laws create variable continuous exposure; arrest can feed custody/harm.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender care banned 27 states; proposed insurance denial; funding freeze; youth crisis services shut; hospital subpoenas. Adult/visitor continuity care not explicitly barred.
care_services.protection: Some orders blocked/enjoined; general emergency care not documented as denied; state protections vary.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking or injury can expose records/ward placement; adult with trans minor faces combined care/school bans.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National removal of gender terminology, funding freeze, school prosecution orders, counterterrorism labels radically pro-transgender, memos reference radical gender ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime statute, employment discrimination precedent, 22 states/province non-discrimination; no documented bounty use against travellers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing can validate border/facility enforcement and reduce perceived recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face youth care bans, social-transition prosecutions, school funding penalties; guardians may share refusal/permanent-fraud exposure if travel blocked.
minors_guardians.protection: Some full-support states; courts block orders; guardianship not otherwise documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult + trans minor layers entry screening, facilities, care and school regimes.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific street violence rate; police exposure appears via border detentions, visa issues, facility arrest and custody abuse.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime law and state bias statutes in 23; many protective jurisdictions; some functional courts.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local response varies; national hostility can affect police and facility staff.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restrictions allowed pending litigation; fraud bar possible but no gender-marker fraud imposition documented; custody claims single-sourced; do-not-travel advocacy criteria unstated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Appeals, lawsuits, legal FAQ, injunctions; hate-crime/employment law remain partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outcomes depend on port/state/officer/court timing; protection may not halt entry or facility enforcement.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A, entry is discretionary and document-driven, but worse: suspected misrepresentation can trigger lifetime fraud ineligibility, and facility/custody policies add criminal detention and abuse risk.
Close to 0.25-C: birth-sex facility and custody harm with limited remedy; but no campaign of cross-dressing arrests and stronger anti-discrimination/hate-crime machinery, so slightly above 0.25.
Above 0.55-B: screening/refusal friction is only lower tier; this regime includes enforceable facility bans, criminal trespass, and immigration/corrections custody abuse.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime layers federal entry and facility restrictions over hostile state laws. Passport binary rules make discovery likely at visa/entry; suspected mismatch can escalate to refusal, investigation, and possible lifetime ineligibility. Facility bans create continuous exposure; a few criminalize use, and one arrest included a men's-ward hold. If custody follows, documented policies and reports indicate hormone removal, forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse. Courts, hate-crime and employment protections provide partial recourse, but institutions are enforcing restrictive rules, so protection does not erase exposure. Rating sits in High Risk, above lethal-imprisonment anchors but well below reduced-risk anchors.
